skills.name: api-contract
skills.description: Design, change or consume an HTTP API without breaking the clients you cannot see. Use when adding endpoints, changing a response shape, introducing versioning, pagination, idempotency or error codes, when a mobile client will lag behind the server, or when a "small" response change has to stay compatible with old builds.

skills.name: bilingual-docs
skills.description: Keep documentation in two languages from drifting apart. Use when a project writes docs in English and another language, when a translated page is out of date or missing, when links and anchors break across locales, when Persian or Arabic (RTL) text mixes with code and numbers, or when a translation reads like machine output rather than an author.

skills.name: debug-connectivity
skills.description: Diagnose why two processes, two machines, a container and its host, or a client and a server cannot exchange traffic. Use when a connection times out or is refused, when a service works locally but not from another host, when a request works on one network and fails on another, or when someone asks to "fix the networking" without a single measurement yet.

skills.name: diagnose-slow
skills.description: Find out what is actually slow before changing any code. Use when a page, endpoint, query, build, test suite or device feels slow, when someone proposes a cache, an index, an async rewrite or a faster library without a measurement, or when a performance problem keeps coming back after a previous "fix".

skills.name: plan-migration
skills.description: Plan a framework, runtime, dependency or schema upgrade that touches many files, without a big-bang rewrite. Use when asked to upgrade to a new major version, replace a library, split a monolith, move a package between repos, or when a previous migration stalled half-finished and left two ways of doing the same thing.

skills.name: release-verify
skills.description: Verify a release artefact before it is announced, and write release notes that do not overclaim. Use when publishing a binary, container image, package, static site or mobile build, when a build "succeeded" but nobody opened it, when checksums or versions are missing, or when a release note needs to state what was and was not tested.

skills.name: review-diff
skills.description: Review a pull request, a patch or an agent's own work with findings ranked by risk instead of listed by line. Use when asked to review a diff, when a change touches data, auth, money, migrations or concurrency, when reviewing generated code that looks plausible, or when a review is turning into a style debate the linter should have settled.

skills.name: write-a-skill
skills.description: Write a new skill for this pack or for any agent: choosing the trigger, structuring the instructions, deciding what belongs in references, and testing whether the skill actually changes behaviour. Use when adding a skill, when an existing skill is not being loaded or is being ignored, or when turning a repeated correction into something an agent will apply by itself.

skills.name: write-postmortem
skills.description: Write a blameless postmortem after an outage, a bad deploy, a data loss or a near miss. Use when an incident needs a written record, when the only finding so far is "human error", when action items keep recurring without owners, or when a team needs a timeline that survives being read six months later.
